container: The gig economy describes a labor market built around short term jobs and freelance tasks rather than permanent employment. Workers may drive passengers, deliver meals, design websites, or provide consulting through digital platforms. This flexibility can help people choose when and where they work and earn income from several sources. Yet gig work often lacks predictable pay, health insurance, paid leave, and retirement benefits. Platforms may also control access to customers and set important rules. Understanding the gig economy means weighing independence against insecurity and recognizing how laws, technology, and worker organizing shape its future.
